title: Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd - 500040 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Birla Estates Q1 FY27 collections rose 31% YoY to Rs 713 crore while net sales were muted at about Rs 329 crore, with no launches in the quarter.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 collections of Rs 713 crore, up 31% from Rs 445 crore a year earlier, and net debt reduced to nearly zero after the Century Pulp and Paper sale to ITC. Net sales were about Rs 329 crore (booking value referenced as Rs 3.3 billion), held back by cancellations and terminations, mainly at Birla Niyaara, with no fresh launches in the quarter. Management added the Vashi redevelopment (GDV about Rs 2,600 crore, 90:10 revenue share), taking the residential redevelopment portfolio to about Rs 4,300 crore. Business development remained slow versus the Rs 10,000–15,000 crore annual target, which management reiterated for FY27 and a Rs 15,000 crore pre-sales ambition over three years.

financial_highlights.change: after Century Pulp and Paper divestment

financial_highlights.value: Rs 437 crore total, of which construction cost about Rs 226 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash outflow from land, capital outflows and deposits
financial_highlights.change: land Rs 125 crore, net deposits Rs 151 crore, capex about Rs 7 crore

segments.name: Birla Taranya (MMR, Thane)
segments.commentary: Booking value above Rs 1,000 crore within the first three months of RERA approval. MMR plotted development at Birla Mrida (Boisar) and Taranya together delivered Rs 150 crore sustenance booking value.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 119 crore booking value from Birla Punya Phase-2 and Birla Evam.

segments.name: Bengaluru (Birla Trimaya Phase-4)
segments.commentary: 91% of inventory launched in the last two quarters already sold.

segments.name: Birla Niyaara (Worli)
segments.commentary: Four cancellations in the quarter (one Tower A, three Tower B), with two rebooked at about Rs 4 crore higher per apartment; Tower B average ticket about Rs 40 crore; 118 net units sold in Phase-2 to date.

segments.name: Residential redevelopment
segments.commentary: Vashi project added with GDV about Rs 2,600 crore; total redevelopment portfolio about Rs 4,300 crore. Margins guided at 25-30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 BD target of Rs 10,000–15,000 crore GDV, described as achievable; no quarterly BD timing given.
Rs 15,000 crore pre-sales in three years reiterated; management declined to guide FY28 specifically.
FY27 launches of about Rs 9,600 crore planned, mostly in Q3 and Q4; management said on track.
FY27 construction cost about Rs 1,200–1,300 crore.
Birla Niyaara large-format launch: RERA expected by end Q2, launch early to mid Q3 FY27.
Vashi project launch targeted Q2 (FY28 per analyst clarification); expected realisation Rs 38,000–40,000 per sq ft on about 1 million sq ft saleable area.
Birla Niyaara Tower C launch price tentatively Rs 100,000–120,000 per sq ft; Tower-1 possession targeted 2027 Q3 within RERA deadline of March 2028, with margins about 40%.
Commercial development of about 1.3 million sq ft at Birla Niyaara to start approvals/construction before end FY27; leasing in about four years, at least Rs 800 crore annual leasing when stabilised.
capex_capacity: Birla Niyaara commercial block: about 1.3 million sq ft; institutional/PE partner under evaluation (IFC or MUFG named by analyst, not decided).
Birla Niyaara large-format launch with fungible options planned, following the Silas format.
Birla Aurora and Birla Centurion together give about Rs 140–150 crore annual rental income, 100% occupied.
Handover of Birla Tisya and phases of Birla Navya in FY27; Birla Niyaara Tower-A possession next year.
Noida Sector 150 land is out of the picture; company is bidding in Noida land auctions and looking at Gurgaon auctions.
demand_pricing: Management said Mumbai premium demand is stable and growing in both price and volume; NCR (Gurgaon, Noida) and Bengaluru are being added.
Pipeline of term sheets and advanced deals above Rs 60,000 crore, split across NCR, Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru, with a Mumbai tilt from redevelopment.
Total GDV pipeline about Rs 74,000 crore, of which about Rs 32,000 crore launched and about Rs 42,000 crore unlaunched.
Price increases taken at Birla Niyaara and Silas Tower-A; Worli premium segment cited as commanding strong premiums.
BD challenges cited: pricing, location, clean title, risk-managed structure, and competitive overbidding.
Most deals are outright acquisitions; more than 50% of portfolio is outright development, with JVs making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Why was net sales of about Rs 329 crore weak when absorption was healthy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to cancellations and terminations for non-payment, mainly at Niyaara, with no launches in the quarter. Gross sales were above Rs 700 crore, and cancelled units were being rebooked at higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 9,600 crore FY27 launch plan on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was largely on track, with most launches planned for Q3 and Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Vashi margins and structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic interest is 90% with a 10% partner, who handles society negotiations and approvals. Margins are expected at 25–30%, with sales at Rs 38,000–40,000 per sq ft on about 1 million sq ft saleable area.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Rs 283 crore cash outflows on the cash flow statement?
qa_highlights.answer: Land payment about Rs 125 crore (Thane), net deposit outflow about Rs 151 crore (including a Noida auction EMD and a Khar redevelopment deposit), and capex about Rs 7 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much construction spend is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said FY27 construction cost would be about Rs 1,200–1,300 crore, against Rs 226 crore construction cost in Q1 out of Rs 437 crore total spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why has BD lagged peers over the past 1.5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a robust risk framework, due diligence, pricing, title and competitive bidding, and said deals negotiated for 18–24 months are close to closing. It described its stance as prudent rather than conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax impact on the ITC proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Tax outflow is expected on the proceeds, but the amount is still being worked out. The balance about 5% of consideration is subject to conditions and working capital adjustments.

risks_watch: Net sales of about Rs 329 crore versus gross sales above Rs 700 crore: track whether cancellations and terminations (mainly Birla Niyaara) reverse in subsequent quarters as management indicated
FY27 launch plan of about Rs 9,600 crore, mostly in Q3 and Q4; Birla Niyaara large-format RERA expected by end Q2 with launch early to mid Q3, so any slippage into FY28 is a key monitor

Business development: FY27 target of Rs 10,000-15,000 crore GDV versus no closed BD in the quarter and a slow 1.5-year record; the Rs 15,000 crore pre-sales goal is now framed as a three-year plan, not FY28
Deployment of surplus cash after net debt fell to nearly zero, with ITC balance about 5% still pending conditions and working capital adjustments, and tax outflow not yet quantified

Construction spend ramp to about Rs 1,200-1,300 crore in FY27 versus Rs 226 crore construction cost in Q1, and commercial development of 1.3 million sq ft at Birla Niyaara with an institutional partner yet to be chosen
key_quotes: Let me assure you that these cancellations we are booking at higher prices.
So, largely, we are more or less on track. Most of the launches are planned for Q3 and Q4.
On an annual basis, I have guided you in the range over Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores is what we are aiming to do in this financial year.
I am not currently commenting on next year. I am confidently commenting on a three-year plan.
I would rather choose the word prudent.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, collections and the Niyaara and Vashi launch plans, but cautious and somewhat defensive on business development, where it repeatedly declined to give quarterly timing and stressed patience and prudence. It was also evasive on FY28 pre-sales growth, guiding only to the three-year Rs 15,000 crore pre-sales ambition.

adds.what: Birla Niyaara commercial block about 1.3 million sq ft (leasing, not yet started; approvals/construction to start before end FY27)
Birla Niyaara large-format launch (residential inventory, RERA expected end Q2, launch early-mid Q3 FY27)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 BD of Rs 10,000-15,000 crore and ~Rs 9,600 crore launches mostly in Q3-Q4, with pipeline of Rs 60,000+ crore in advanced talks, but no firm BD orders are cited, Q1 net sales were muted at ~Rs 329 crore due to Niyaara cancellations, and no revenue growth % was given.
